clue.text: Two adults run ahead and catch country composer

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for adult, twice
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
to be ahead is to be on, as in going on
to cop is slang for to catch
a land is a country

explanation.surface: Two grown-ups race off to catch a composer of country music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country composer' reads as a writer of country songs; the words split, with 'country' giving letters and 'composer' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron Copland was the American composer of Appalachian Spring and Fanfare for the Common Man.

clue.text: Description of noon correct?

blocks.note: noon is the morning's close

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an account of midday is accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: AM is the morning and noon is where it stops, so noon can be described as the AM END.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text is to correct it, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Adjust bottom line

blocks.note: the rear is the bottom, the backside
a range is a line, as of hills or products

explanation.surface: An instruction to tweak the lowest line of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange is to change the order of things, which is a way to adjust them.

clue.text: Most intimate war god seen in lace

indicators.note: something seen in a fabric sits inside it, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: net is an open lacy fabric
Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: A god of battle at his most private, glimpsed through lace curtains.
explanation.walkthrough: The war god sits between the first two letters of the fabric and its last.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearest and dearest: the nearest people are the closest, most intimate ones.

clue.text: Something that circles gold tooth?

blocks.note: or is gold in heraldry
a tooth is something that bites, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A puzzled look at whether a gold tooth goes round in circles.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful idea of a tooth as a biter.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbiter is a spacecraft or body that travels round a planet in orbit.

clue.text: Parrot in transport leaving a river

indicators.note: something leaving departs, so those letters go out of the word

blocks.note: a lorry is a British truck, a means of transport
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A parrot travels in a vehicle that drives away from a river.
explanation.walkthrough: One R of LORRY, the British word for a truck, goes, leaving LORY.
explanation.definitionFit: A lory is a small brightly coloured parrot of Australasia, a kind of lorikeet.

clue.text: Crackers I turn to in food processing?

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters following are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone resorts to crackers as food, perhaps while working a food processor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crackers' looks like a snack in a food scene, but it is the anagram signal. 'Food processing?' is not the kitchen gadget but the body's handling of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutrition is the process by which an organism takes in food and uses it, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Steal our cash? Time to be strong

blocks.note: to steal our cash is to rob us
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Faced with theft of the takings, it is time to stand firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows 'Steal our cash' is a playful paraphrase of a two-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust means sturdy and vigorous, an ordinary adjective synonym.

clue.text: Composer needs one to stop "Scottish Dvorak" working with him

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so a letter is put into the words in quotes
working suggests things being worked over and refashioned into a new order

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer needs a single colleague to block a rival dubbed the Scottish Dvorak from collaborating with him.
explanation.walkthrough: Since everything is then reshuffled, where the one goes does not matter; it simply joins the letters of the quoted nickname and him.
explanation.definitionFit: Dmitri Shostakovich was the Soviet composer of fifteen symphonies.

clue.text: Love major character from Greece

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
mega means huge, major

explanation.surface: Romance with a leading figure from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so a Greek character.

clue.text: Rook tolerated in a corporation's botanic garden

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the first pair go within the next words

blocks.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook
to bore something is to put up with it, as in bore the pain
a corporation is old jokey British slang for a paunch, a tum; the 's is the link

explanation.surface: A rook is allowed into a company's botanical garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company but is old British slang for a large belly.
explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a garden devoted to growing trees for study and display.

clue.text: Chat here and there with NUS refreshed air

indicators.note: refreshed means given a new form, so these letters are made over into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; NUS is the National Union of Students

explanation.surface: Mingling and chatting with the students' union in the fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' sounds like the open air of the surface, but it means a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Underneath the Arches is a famous music-hall song by Flanagan and Allen, and an air is a song.

clue.text: Heard, not seen, in fog

indicators.note: heard means the word that follows is taken as spoken, by its sound

blocks.note: something not seen has been missed

explanation.surface: Something heard but invisible in a fog.
explanation.definitionFit: Mist is a thin fog of tiny water droplets, a near synonym.

clue.text: Ball on head turned cup tie

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the word for the trophy is read from the other end

blocks.note: a pot is slang for a sports trophy
a knot is a tie

explanation.surface: A football commentary: a header turns a cup tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ball on head' and 'cup tie' paint a football match; the ball is hair, and a cup tie is a knockout match.
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is hair gathered into a bun or ball on top of the head.

clue.text: Boozer with French name, writer hot in Asian city

blocks.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house; a boozer is British slang for a pub
nom is French for name
a pen writes
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A drinker with a French name and a hot-tempered writer in an Asian city.
explanation.walkthrough: A boozer is British slang for a pub, abbreviated PH on maps.
explanation.definitionFit: Phnom Penh is the capital city of Cambodia in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Chopin is so remiss holding back composer

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer within it, spread across its words
back means the held letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the run of letters from the end of the first word into the last

explanation.surface: One composer accuses another of slacking by holding something back.
explanation.walkthrough: Another composer's name, Chopin, starts the clue, tempting the solver to treat it as the definition; it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian composer of The Barber of Seville and William Tell.

clue.text: Plain ties with green buckles

indicators.note: something that buckles bends out of shape, so these letters are distorted

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Simple neckties fastened with green buckles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective for the ties, but it is a noun: flat grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a vast plain of grassland in Tanzania, famed for its wildlife migration.

clue.text: Line with curve in bronze by refined man

blocks.note: tan is a bronze colour, as of suntanned skin
a gent is a gentleman, a refined man

explanation.surface: A cultured man in bronze, drawing lines and curves.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a tangent is a straight line that touches a curve at one point.

clue.text: Warm to a place of debauchery?

blocks.note: taken as written
a sty is a pigsty, figuratively a place of debauchery

explanation.surface: Someone warms to a den of vice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warm to' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'Warm' alone is the definition and 'to' is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Toasty is an informal adjective meaning pleasantly warm, as by a fire.

clue.text: Windpipe long in exotic rat

indicators.note: exotic means strange and foreign, so the letters of the rodent are made unfamiliar
one word in another sits inside it, so the yearning goes within the rodent's letters

blocks.note: the letters of rat rearranged
to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: A strange rat has a long windpipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exotic' works only on the rodent, and the reshuffled animal then wraps the longing; the surface's 'long' looks like a description of the windpipe.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the anatomical name for the windpipe, the tube carrying air to the lungs.

clue.text: Doctor trepans mum and dad

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A surgeon bores holes in the skulls of a mother and father.
explanation.walkthrough: To trepan is to drill a hole in the skull; 'Doctor' looks like the surgeon but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mum and dad are, together, a child's parents.

clue.text: Artist in devout company round holy mount

indicators.note: something placed round another encloses it, so the firm's letters wrap the animal

blocks.note: pi is informal for pious, devout
Co is the abbreviation for company
the donkey Jesus rode into Jerusalem, a holy steed

explanation.surface: A painter among a pious group gathered round a sacred mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a mountain, but it is a creature ridden: the ass of Palm Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism.

clue.text: Soothsayer's written about teetotaller in Sun?

indicators.note: a word written about another is set around it, enclosing it

blocks.note: a seer foretells the future, as a soothsayer does
TT is the abbreviation for teetotal, a non-drinker

explanation.surface: A newspaper astrologer writes about a non-drinker in the Sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, which tempts a newspaper reading; the definition instead treats the sun as something that sets each evening.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun sets daily, so it is playfully a setter; the question mark marks this as a pun.

clue.text: Top wizard rakes in million

indicators.note: someone who rakes in money gathers it inside, so the large number goes within

blocks.note: a wizard at something is an ace
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A top-class wizard earns a million.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the peak or highest point of something.

clue.text: Litres in French and Spanish wines for grouch

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the unit goes within the French wine

blocks.note: Macon is a French wine from Burgundy
L is the abbreviation for litres
tent is an old name for a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A sour person orders litres of French and Spanish wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wines' does double duty for both nations; tent is an archaic word for a dark Spanish wine, from tinto.
explanation.definitionFit: A malcontent is a perpetually dissatisfied complainer, a grouch.

clue.text: World Famine Day cancelled

indicators.note: something cancelled is struck off, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: a dearth is a scarcity or famine
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A global day highlighting hunger has been called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'World Famine Day' reads as a charity event name; 'World' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is our planet, the world we live on.

clue.text: Lover-boy among white roses

indicators.note: among means sitting within the following words, so the letters are found inside them

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A romantic young man stands among white roses.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, the winged boy known in Rome as Cupid.

clue.text: See 11
Eastern end of the lake spooky

blocks.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: The east side of the lake is creepy.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and unsettling, a near synonym for spooky.
